stop_condition: Every claim the fix rests on is independently measured — (a) that disabling globasciiranges reproduces macOS bash 3.2 collation semantics rather than manufacturing a condition no real host has, (b) that the SHIPPED explicit-class guard is provably NOT helped by the shopt, (c) that 13w.0 and the non-vacuity legs can actually FAIL when mutated, (d) that a locale-less host still skips with a message naming the real prerequisite — and no critical/high finding remains in section 13w ability to detect a regression of dolt_hash_looks_valid, nor any weakening of STRICT_SECTIONS.

findings.evidence: The probe is `if bash -c 'shopt -p globasciiranges' >/dev/null 2>&1`, which keys on EXIT STATUS. Measured (cwp-l1-repro:1.1.2, bash 5.2.21; and macOS bash 3.2.57, at bcd5396): present+SET -> stdout='shopt -s globasciiranges', exit 0; present+UNSET (`shopt -u globasciiranges; shopt -p globasciiranges`) -> stdout='shopt -u globasciiranges', exit 1; ABSENT (bash 3.2) -> stdout='', exit 1. So exit status cannot separate 'absent' from 'present but already unset' — only stdout can.
findings.description: The probe tests 'the option exists AND is currently set', not 'the option exists'. The comment directly above it claims the opposite in terms: 'The probe below detects CAPABILITY (does this bash even have the option?), never a bash version number, so a future bash that changes the default again is still handled correctly.' FUNCTIONAL IMPACT: none — when the option is present-but-unset, ranges are already locale-sensitive, so the empty preamble is the correct behaviour and the section still works. DIAGNOSTIC IMPACT: on such a host the precondition line at :2815 prints 'no globasciiranges option on this bash (pre-4.3, e.g. macOS shipped bash 3.2); collation applies unconditionally', which is false about that host. globasciiranges was introduced in bash 4.3 defaulting OFF and only flipped ON in 5.0, so bash 4.3/4.4 hosts hit exactly this branch. Neither supported platform does (macOS 3.2 = genuinely absent; CI ubuntu 5.2.21 = present and set), which is why this is LOW and not blocking. It is recorded because this task exists BECAUSE a precondition message misstated its own cause, and the replacement can misstate the host's bash in the same lines. VERIFIED ONE-LINE FIX: key on stdout instead — `if [ -n "$(bash -c 'shopt -p globasciiranges' 2>/dev/null)" ]; then` — true for both 'shopt -s' and 'shopt -u' output, false when the option does not exist.

findings.description: The change was authored and committed without a delegated specialist spawn, so no F7 completion contract was recorded. CLAUDE.md names this as an antipattern ('Don't have the orchestrator write code directly ... delegate to a specialist agent'). Consequence for the gate: `qa-gate.sh approve` refuses with error_key=completion_record_missing, and qa.md section 10 forbids QA satisfying that refusal with its own contract (QA's files_changed is [] and would defeat the completeness cross-check's independent witness). qa.md prescribes the audited `--no-completion '<reason>'` exit for the 'there was genuinely no specialist' case, which is what this review takes, with the reason naming that. Not HIGH: it is an audit-trail gap, not a defect in the shipped change, and the gate forces an explicit recorded decision rather than silently passing. Recorded so the missing contract is visible rather than inferred from an absence.

findings.description: `.diff` is git diff HEAD-vs-working-tree, so for an ALREADY-COMMITTED change under review it is empty by construction — the commonest shape for a review that runs after the implementer commits, which is exactly this task's shape. The honest note names two candidate causes and omits that one, so a reviewer consuming only the request gets zero bytes of the change plus a misdirecting hint. This review compensated by reading `git show bcd5396` directly, but a Sol-lane review over the request alone would have reviewed nothing. Tooling finding against wuu8, not against 8lc1; worth a follow-up task to add the committed-change case to the note (and, ideally, to fall back to HEAD-vs-parent when the working tree is clean).
